newsitem.title: UK: Copper surplus seen at 240,000 T in 1997 - Brandeis.
newsitem.headline: Copper surplus seen at 240,000 T in 1997 - Brandeis.

text.p: Copper supply in the Western world is forecast to outstrip demand by 240,000 tonnes in 1997 after a surplus of 100,000 tonnes in 1996, according to broker Brandeis in its daily base metals review.
The growing surplus follows two years of deficits, with the 1994 shortfall pegged at 248,000 tonnes and that in 1995 at 48,000 tonnes.

Brandeis forecast refined output in the Western world to rise to 10.2 million tonnes next year from 9.75 million this year. Net imports into the West were expected to be stable at 700,000 tonnes for both years.
Western consumption was pegged at 10.66 million tonnes in 1997, up three percent from 10.35 million in 1996.
Brandeis predicted three month copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) would average $2,050 a tonne in 1997 from $2,300 in 1996 and $2,864 in 1995.

Also in its daily metals review, Flemings Global Mining Group said world producer stocks of copper rose to 668,000 tonnes by the end of June this year, up 16 percent from end-1995 levels of 574,000 tonnes. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
